articles.title: Cold Winds Bring Cooler Days to Taiwan
articles.zh: 東北季風報到，台灣變冷了

source.name: Focus Taiwan：Northeasterly winds to send mercury down to 11°C later this week

articles.note: 依本週新聞改寫成 A2-B1 學習文章，非原文。
paras: Winter is coming to Taiwan. This week, the weather agency said that strong northeasterly winds would bring a sharp drop in temperatures from Wednesday to Friday.
In northern Taiwan and Yilan, daytime highs fell from about 25 to 27 degrees on Wednesday to only 18 to 20 degrees on Thursday. In some low areas, the lowest temperature could reach about 11 degrees.
The good news is that most of the island will stay dry. If you go out early in the morning or late at night, wear a warm jacket and drink something hot.

winter.def: the coldest season of the year
winter.g: Winter is coming 冬天要來了（現在進行式表示即將發生）。

agency.def: a government office that does a special job

bring.def: to make something happen or come
bring.g: 過去式 brought；文中 would bring 是轉述未來。

temperature.def: how hot or cold something is
temperature.g: a drop in temperatures 氣溫下降。

fell.g: fall-fell-fallen；highs fell from… to… 從…降到…。

dry.g: stay dry 保持乾燥、不下雨。

grammar.zh: 轉述別人的話時，will 常變成 would。
grammar.ex: the weather agency said that strong northeasterly winds would bring a sharp drop in temperatures
If you go out early in the morning or late at night, wear a warm jacket

questions.q: How low could the temperature go in some low areas?
What will the weather be like on most of the island?

keySentences.s: The good news is that most of the island will stay dry.

articles.title: A World Stamp Show Opens in Taipei

source.name: Focus Taiwan：Rare Stamps Take Center Stage as Taipei World Stamp Exhibition Opens November 20

articles.note: 依本週新聞改寫成 A2-B1 學習文章，非原文。
paras: A big world stamp show opened in Taipei on November 20. It runs until November 25 at the Taipei World Trade Center, and visitors can enter for free.

One famous stamp at the show is the "Inverted Jenny" from 1918. Because of a printing mistake, the plane on the stamp is upside down. Collectors have loved this rare stamp for more than a hundred years.
The show also celebrates 130 years of Chunghwa Post. Its theme is innovation and sustainability. Some new Pokémon stamps were so popular that most of them sold out before the show began.

stamp.def: a small piece of paper you put on a letter

visitor.def: a person who visits a place

enter.g: enter for free 免費入場。

printing.def: making words or pictures on paper with a machine

upside down.def: with the top part at the bottom
upside down.g: 片語，放在 be 動詞後。

rare.g: this rare stamp 這張稀有郵票。

celebrate.def: to do something special for an important event
celebrate.g: celebrates 130 years 慶祝 130 週年。

theme.def: the main idea of an event
theme.ex: The theme of the party is the sea.
theme.g: Its theme is… 它的主題是…。

grammar.ex: It runs until November 25 at the Taipei World Trade Center
Because of a printing mistake, the plane on the stamp is upside down.
Some new Pokémon stamps were so popular that most of them sold out before the show began.

questions.q: How much does it cost to enter the show?
What is special about the Inverted Jenny?
What happened to many Pokémon stamps?

keySentences.s: Its theme is innovation and sustainability.
The show also celebrates 130 years of Chunghwa Post.

articles.title: A Weekly Trip to the Park Helps Children
articles.zh: 每週去公園，孩子更健康

source.name: University of Bristol：Going to the park at least once a week can improve children's mental health

articles.note: 依本週新聞改寫成 A2-B1 學習文章，非原文。
paras: A new study from the UK says that going to the park can be good for children's minds. Children who visited parks and playgrounds at least once a week had better mental health as they grew up.

Researchers used information about more than 4,000 children from a long study called Children of the 90s. Children who went to the park every week, from birth to age 11, scored about 16.5 percent better on mental health tests.
Parks give children space to run, play and use their imagination. This can build confidence. The researchers say that cities need safe parks that are open to all families.

park.def: a public green area in a town
park.g: go to the park 去公園。

mind.def: the part of a person that thinks and feels

playground.def: an outdoor area where children play

researcher.def: a person who studies something carefully

score.def: to get points in a test or game

imagination.def: the ability to make new pictures in your mind
imagination.ex: Children have a lot of imagination.
imagination.g: use their imagination 發揮想像力。

grammar.zh: going to the park 當主詞。
grammar.ex: going to the park can be good for children's minds
Children who went to the park every week

questions.q: How often should children visit parks, according to the study?
How many children were in the study?
What do the researchers say cities need?

keySentences.s: Parks give children space to run, play and use their imagination.
The researchers say that cities need safe parks that are open to all families.

articles.title: How to make stress your friend

source.name: TED：Kelly McGonigal, How to make stress your friend

articles.note: 內容主題取自 TED 熱門演講。內文為學習用改寫，不是講者原話，請看原演講了解細節。
paras: Stress can make your heart beat fast and your hands sweat. Many people think stress is always bad for them. In this popular TED talk, health psychologist Kelly McGonigal looks at stress in a new way.
She shares research that suggests stress may be bad for us mainly when we believe it is harmful. So the way we think about stress can change how our body reacts to it.
She also talks about a simple way to handle stress: reach out to other people. When life is hard, asking a friend for help, or helping someone else, can make us stronger.

stress.def: a feeling of worry because of problems

heart.g: make your heart beat：make + 受詞 + 原形。

psychologist.def: a person who studies the mind

research.def: careful study to find new facts

react.g: reacts to it 對它起反應。

grammar.ex: Stress can make your heart beat fast
the way we think about stress can change how our body reacts to it
asking a friend for help, or helping someone else, can make us stronger

questions.q: What can stress make your heart do?
When may stress be bad for us, according to the research?
opts: When we believe it is harmful

questions.q: What simple way to handle stress does she suggest?

keySentences.s: Many people think stress is always bad for them.
Stress can make your heart beat fast and your hands sweat.
